newsitem.title: USA: US spot LPGs track NYMEX futures down, late trade.
newsitem.headline: US spot LPGs track NYMEX futures down, late trade.

text.p: U.S. liquefied petroleum gas prices tracked NYMEX futures in their afternoon slide on Wednesday, players said, with the Midwest faring better than the U.S. Gulf Coast.
In late trade, spot propane in the U.S. Gulf Coast fell about a half cent to between 34.25 cents and 34.50 cents a gallon after shedding a quarter cent midday.
The decline came following the slide in NYMEX crude oil futures, which ended down 72 cents at $19.54 a barrel after IPE Brent broke key technical support.
"We nosedived when crude started to fall," said one Houston-based trader.
Conway, Kansas, material resisted the bath better, shedding about a quarter cent to 35.00/35.25 cents due to moderate activity by end users.
The natural gasoline market also slipped on NYMEX gasoline futures, which ended down 2.06 cents at 60.61 cents a gallon.
Belvieu natural was assessed at 45.00/45.25, Conway material was about 42.50/43.00 cents.
Belvieu purity ethane traded at 19.00 cents and ethane mix at 18.00 cents. ((--Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1631))
